recommendation: Run a 2-quarter pilot in Germany (Mittelstand logistics + retail in North Rhine-Westphalia and Bavaria) before committing build-out. Park France as a phase-2 expansion contingent on pilot KPIs.
summary: Germany offers the larger absolute opportunity (€18.4B vs France's smaller market), denser ICP clustering, and stickier post-landing economics (117% NRR), but with longer procurement cycles (7.2 months vs 4.8). France grows faster (22% YoY) and is cheaper to staff but the public-sector tailwind is harder to capture with a 12-person team. A sequenced single-country entry beats parallel at this headcount; an anchor-pilot in Germany de-risks the more capital-intensive bet first. Two diligence gates conditioning the full build-out: confirmed unit economics in one reference vertical, and a signed compliance pathway for in-country data residency.
key_reasons: Germany's B2B SaaS market is roughly 1.6x larger than France's, with denser mid-market logistics and retail clusters in NRW and Bavaria.
Net revenue retention is structurally higher in German Mittelstand (117%) than French mid-market (109%) — stickier once landed.
Sequenced single-country entry produces 2.3x the qualified pipeline at this team size compared to parallel entry.
A 2-quarter pilot reliably resolves go/no-go on full entry economics, lowering the cost of being wrong about Germany.
France's faster growth and lower cost-of-presence are real, but the public-sector framework that drives much of it is hard to capture with 12 headcount.
GDPR data-residency expectations are stricter in German RFPs (68% vs 41%), which the pilot must validate compliance pathways for early.
risks: German procurement cycles (7.2 months avg) may exceed the pilot window if anchor accounts are picked poorly.
Web-sourced market sizing lags real-time filings; treat absolute numbers as directional until validated against named target accounts.
Two claims rest on partial document coverage (Mittelstand cluster density and pilot success base rates) — see verifier panel.
Choosing Germany defers French public-sector tailwind capture; a 6-month delay may compound if competitors land first.
counterarguments: France-first is defensible if the team has stronger French-language GTM talent — language fit can compress procurement faster than market size advantages.
If the product has a public-sector wedge, France's UGAP framework could be a faster path to revenue than Mittelstand land-and-expand.
Parallel entry is rarely defensible at 12 headcount, but a 'discovery presence' (1-2 advisors) in France during the German pilot is cheap insurance.
next_steps: Define pilot KPIs: 6 named anchor accounts, 2 design partners, signed compliance pathway by month 4.
Stand up data-residency review with counsel; pre-clear in-country hosting options before first RFP.
Recruit a Munich- or Düsseldorf-based founding GTM hire with Mittelstand network.
Gate decision on France build-out to month 6 pilot review; do not pre-commit headcount.
Run a 1-page weekly pipeline review against the 6 named anchors to detect cycle slippage early.
caveats: This report contains 1 inference-supported claim (pilot success base rates). Two claims rest on partial document coverage and are flagged in the verifier panel. Web-sourced market sizing should be validated against named-account RFPs before full build-out commitment.

executive_insights.text: Germany is the larger and stickier market; France grows faster but is harder to capture at 12 headcount.
Sequenced entry beats parallel; an anchor-pilot in Germany resolves the bigger bet first.
Compliance posture (data residency) is the gating risk to pre-clear during the pilot.

key_risks_structured.text: Procurement cycle length may exceed pilot window without disciplined anchor-account selection.
Data-residency expectations may force architecture changes; surface during pilot, not after.

options_matrix.cons: public-sector wedge hard at 12 HC, smaller TAM
halves bandwidth, 2.3x worse pipeline at this HC

kill_criteria: If 0 of 6 anchor accounts move to LOI by month 5, kill Germany-first and re-plan.
If data-residency review uncovers >€500k unforecasted hosting cost, escalate before month 4 commit.
If competitor lands a flagship Mittelstand customer before month 3, re-evaluate ICP segmentation.
what_would_change_our_mind: Direct evidence from named-account RFPs in the target verticals showing French procurement cycles longer than reported, or Mittelstand procurement cycles shorter; either inverts the sequencing logic. Strong existing French-language GTM bench would also weight toward France-first.
